image_description:
## 1) Chart type
- **Top:** Pictogram / icon-based ranked grid of teams, with repeated sandwich icons representing quantity.
- **Bottom:** **Scatter plot**.

## 2) Layout techniques
- **Top:** Uses a **small-multiples/grid layout** of team panels. No stacking in the chart sense; quantity is shown by repeated icons within each panel.
- **Bottom:** Single-panel scatter plot with points positioned by two quantitative axes. No faceting or stacking.

## 3) Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| NFL team (abbreviation/logo) | Categorical/nominal | Small-multiple panel identity; team logo/image; text label |
| Weekly Uncrustables consumed | Quantitative | Text value in each team panel; repeated sandwich icons/area/count in top panel; x-axis position in scatter plot |
| NFL standings (win-loss-tie percentage) | Quantitative | y-axis position in scatter plot |
| Sandwich unit key (“= 10”) | Quantitative scale annotation | Legend/key using one sandwich icon plus label |

comments.raw_comment:
I notice that Denver seems to eat a much higher amount of uncrustables than every other NFL team, including their closest neighboring teams - geography wise.  I also notice that a lot of the teams that do eat the most uncrustables every week (excluding Denver) are mostly coastal cities, like Seattle, Charlotte, Miami, and NY.

What I wonder is if higher elevation has something to do with the intake of sweeter foods.  While the big coastal cities may intake a lot of uncrustables by the week, they are exactly that, coastal cities.  Denver, on the other hand, holds a massive height above sea level, an incredibly different environment from many other cities on the list.  Many sweet foods take time to prepare and serve, unlike uncrustables, which a team could grab in between practices with ease.  I also wonder if Denver gets its uncrustables directly from the source.  I googled where the main manufacturers of uncrustables are located, and one of the two main manufacturers is located only 38 miles away from where the Broncos practice and play.

While there aren't many uncrustable related things in my community, I know that my family and I will feel safer at night knowing that when the Broncos do play again, they will be charging onto the field in a fit of perpetual, Peanut Butter and Jelly - induced rage.

This graph demonstrates the number of Uncrustables consumed by different NFL teams weekly in 2023. I first noticed this graph's sheer absurdity, but the more I analyzed it, the more sense it made. I assume they are eating peanut butter and jelly sandwiches, which are high in protein and good fats because of the peanut butter. I also noticed that the Denver Broncos eat the most Uncrustables by a lot, and when I researched their winning percentage this season, it was .615. The team with the least amount of Uncrustables eaten is the New Orleans Saints, with a win percentage of .385. I wonder if the weekly Uncrustables consumption can directly impact a team's skills. I also wonder what makes Uncrustables universally the best choice. Is it their small size yet high nutrition value? This relates to my community because I am a lifelong New York Giants fan, and I wonder if increasing their Uncrustable intake could help them improve their skills (because they need some improvement). I am curious because, as I previously mentioned, the Denver Broncos have a win percentage of .615, whereas the New York Giants have a percentage of .154 this season. I wonder if increasing their UPW (Uncrustables Per Week) could help them not be horrible.

comments.raw_comment:
Headline- Uncrustables: The Real MVP of the NFL
This graph illustrates the weekly Uncrustable consumption across NFL teams, with each Uncrustable displayed representing 10 actual sandwiches. I notice that the Denver Broncos consume the most, at 700 per week, while the Saints and Bengals consume the least, at 50 per week. Most teams seem to fall somewhere between 100 and 300 Uncrustables per week. Looking at the second graph, I notice that there’s no clear relationship between the number of Uncrustables eaten and a team’s win-loss percentage. However, teams consuming around 100 Uncrustables seem to land somewhere around 50%. 
I wonder why the Broncos eat so many Uncrustables? Are they handed out on the sidelines of practices and games, or are they just the team's favorite snack?  I also wonder if the winning or losses really have anything to do with the amount of Uncrustables they eat. 
This relates to me and my community because I play a sport at my high school. We are always getting snacks such as chips and oranges to get our energy up at half-time. It’s interesting to think about how food can play a role in both professional and school-level sports. It makes me wonder if we ate Uncrustables, we would win more.

This graph shows the tie between Uncrustable intake and NFL teams. I noticed that there is not necessarily a correlation between a high/low consumption rate and a higher/lower win rate. For example, the Denver Broncos consume 700 Uncrustables a week but only have a win percentage of 45%. However, the Kansas City Chiefs consume 80 a week and have a win percentage of around 70-80%. I also noticed that most teams consume under 200 Uncrustables a week. I wonder why Uncrustables are such a common snack in the NFL and what makes them beneficial for hard-working athletes. I also wonder when exactly these started becoming common in the NFL. Was it in the last decade, or has it been a longer tradition? Finally, I'm curious when these players are eating them. Is it during a game, post-game, throughout practice, etc? This applies to my community because I am an athlete, and we usually eat before practice(a quick snack), and this makes me curious if I should replace that snack with an Uncrustable(is there a benefit in doing so?).

This graph showcases the weekly consumption of Uncrustables across the NFL teams in the 2023 season.  The first thing I noticed was the number of Uncrustables consumed by the Denver Broncos, at 700 per week, which was over double the number of Uncrustables consumed by the Seattle Seahawks, at 320 per week.  I wonder why the Broncos have consumed a far greater amount than the rest of the teams.  I also noticed that the Bengals and the Saints consumed 50 Uncrustables per week, in last place.  I also noticed that the Denver Broncos' win-loss-tie percentage is around 50%, while many teams that consume less Uncrustables weekly have higher win-loss-tie percentages.  I wonder why exactly Uncrustables became the new halftime snack for the NFL, and why the Denver Broncos consume so many of them weekly.  I also wonder if the number of Uncrustables consumed truly affects the NFL teams' win-loss-tie percentage.  This relates to me and my community because my family and I are football fans, and it is interesting to see an unusual statistic about Uncrustables in the NFL.

comments.raw_comment:
I notice that while the Denver Broncos consume the most Uncrustables—700 per week—their win percentage doesn’t seem to correlate with this high snack intake. In fact, teams with win rates above 70% typically eat fewer than 200 Uncrustables per week, showing little connection between snack consumption and performance. Many lower-performing teams (with win rates under 40%) also consume fewer Uncrustables, with Denver being the main outlier. This suggests that Uncrustables may be more tied to team culture or logistics rather than directly influencing a team’s success. I wonder why these teams prefer Uncrustables, and what led to the shift from the traditional halftime snack of oranges to something like Uncrustables. I also wonder what other factors, such as practice routines or team dynamics, contribute to a team’s win percentage, aside from snacks. Given the size and physical demands of football players, I also wonder how many Uncrustables each player consumes—since they likely need more than just one or two to feel full. This relates to my community and me because in local teams and sports, everyone has a game-time snack, but that doesn’t necessarily correlate with success. For example, on my high school soccer team, we had Gatorade and chips at halftime, but we rarely won. This shows that snacks, while important, might not be the key factor in determining performance.

Catchy headline: "Uncrustables and NFL Wins: Do Snacks Really Shape Success?"

Observations - Graph #1 shows the approximate ranges for weekly Uncrustables eaten across 24 NFL teams. One uncrustable icon is equal to 10, and a bitten crustable is equal to 5. DEN has the highest amount of weekly Uncrustables eaten, followed by SEA & JAX. Graph #2 shows the No. of Uncrustables eaten per week and the win-loss-tie % in NFL standings. It seems like teams perform best when they eat a moderate amount of Uncrustables, around 50-200 per week, as the largest cluster of Uncrustables is located within the win-loss-tie percentages of 50-80. There is one massive outlier, a team eating 700 a week, and I guess we could say they really like Uncrustables because wow. 

Questions - Can we associate eating a moderate amount of Uncrustables with having a higher win-loss-tie percentage? Is it safe to say it boosts athletic performance for the players? Eating Uncrustables could also be seen as a fun little tradition within schools across the state.
